chase_cards.name: No.1 Trainer
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a regional champion object at the moment Battle Road Summer 2002 becomes more than a venue circuit. The card records a named winner and conference, then points outward toward the Best in Japan structure and, for junior winners, the International Tropical Mega Battle path.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Collector references pin Ken Sugimori to this Battle Road Summer 2002 No.1 Trainer row, while Bulbapedia's No.1 Trainer page places the 2000-2002 regional-trophy illustration lineage in the Ken Sugimori era and Bulbapedia's Sugimori page supplies the broader franchise-art context. The credit is useful, but it remains collector-reference-supported until stronger row-level print proof is attached.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 regional first place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.1 Trainer at source index 250.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.1 Trainer e-Card Era print was awarded to champions of each regional Battle Road Summer 2002 tournament, held between July and August 2002.

Bulbapedia's Elite Four Trainer page gives the Battle Road Summer 2002 regional schedule as Hokkaido on July 20, Tohoku on July 24, Kanto on July 27-28, Chubu on July 31, Kansai on August 3-4, Chugoku/Shikoku on August 9, and Kyushu on August 11, followed by finals in Tokyo on August 17.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series was the first to introduce the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.1 Trainer versions were the last to include the winner's name and regional conference on the card itself and the last to feature male and female variants.
Bulbapedia gives the No.1 Trainer tournament text as recognizing and praising the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament's champion.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Summer 2002 No.1 Trainer page lists Ken Sugimori as illustrator; this is useful collector-reference support, not primary-source print authority.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Summer 2002 No.1 Trainer page lists the distribution date range as July 20 through August 11, 2002.

Pokumon's Battle Road 2002 research reconstructs Summer 2002 No.1 Trainer distribution as 3 girls and 24 boys from Trainers Magazine winner data; this is a collector estimate, not an official copy count.

Pokumon says Summer 2002 winners received a black folio containing the trophy card and certificate, with gold embossing rather than the Spring dark-blue/silver presentation; organizers collected folios after photos and mailed personalized cards back later in September 2002.
Bulbapedia says Battle Road Summer 2002, unlike Spring, culminated in a Best in Japan final with a new card awarded to top ranking players.

Pokumon says Junior league winners of Battle Road Summer 2002 were invited to the International Tropical Mega Battle 2002 in Hawaii, and that the numbered regional Trainer cards from Battle Road Spring and Summer 2002 were the final No.1-No.3 Trainers given away at a regional level before numbered Trainer trophies moved to World Championships.

Bulbapedia's Ken Sugimori page says there are many Pokémon TCG cards illustrated by Sugimori, though most include reused artwork from games, and indexes his broad official artwork role in the franchise.

As judged collector texture, this No.1 Trainer matters because it is a champion card at a hinge in the apparatus: venue, rank, name, conference, folio, mail-back, finals eligibility, and international invitation all press into one object.

Agents should preserve No.1 rank, Battle Road Summer 2002 regional first-place route, source index 250, July 20-August 11 distribution window, e-Card Era layout, winner name and regional conference fields, male/female variant boundary, black folio/gold-embossing provenance, Summer-vs-Spring distinction, and non-equivalence with Best in Japan photo cards, Elite Four Trainer, No.2/No.3 Trainer, Worlds, Neo Road, or other No.1 Trainer eras before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 No.1 Trainer: the champion card at the hinge
narrative.why_it_matters: This No.1 Trainer has the clean thrill of a champion card, but the better story is the machinery around it. Summer 2002 was not only a bracket; it was a moving festival circuit, a point economy, a folio on stage, a card pulled back for personalization, a September return in the mail, and a route onward to Best in Japan or even Hawaii. The card asks an agent to respect contact: who won, where they won, which variant they received, what folio surrounded it, and which later trophy lane it is not.

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer, Summer 2002: a champion card with a return address
narrative.why_it_matters: The card is easy to flatten into a grail, but its real force is procedural and personal. A child or adult won a regional table, stood for the photo with a folio, had the prize taken back so the name could be added, and received the finished recognition later. That delay matters. It turns the card from a generic first-place emblem into a mailed-back memory of a specific winner, conference, body variant, and route through Pokémon's 2002 organized-play machine.
